newsitem.title: FRANCE: Jailed French ex-mayor on hunger strike.
newsitem.headline: Jailed French ex-mayor on hunger strike.

text.p: The ex-mayor of the French Riviera resort of Cannes has begun a hunger strike to demand his release from 10-month-old pre-trial custody in a corruption probe, his lawyer said on Wednesday.
Michel Mouillot was detained after being placed under investigation in July last year over accusations he solicited bribes in exchange for permits to install one-arm bandits in a hotel casino.
"There is no other example of such long pre-trial custody in political corruption cases," said Mouillot's lawyer Francois Saint-Pierre, who has repeatedly asked the courts to release his client.

Mouillot resigned as mayor in February after the Supreme Court upheld an 18-month prison sentence he was given for receiving a fictitious salary from a Lyon businessman. He was also barred from holding public office for five years.

He was placed under investigation again last March on suspicion he illicitly received more than 10 million francs ($1.75 million) in corporate funds channeled through a real estate firm headed by one of his associates.
